facts.fact: Law No. 46, published in the Official Bulletin of 5 April 2026, charges the Directorate of Population Registration and Civil Status Statistics Services, under the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation and headed by a Registrar General the minister appoints, with creating and running a digital registration system with a central database for births, deaths, marriages, divorces and adoptions, and reserves the management of its data to the Directorate alone (articles 10 and 11).

systems.country_label: nidaamka dad-dhigista iyo tirakoobka xaaladaha madaniga ah
systems.owner: Directorate of Population Registration and Civil Status Statistics Services (Agaasinka), Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation
systems.tiers: as the law sets the structure: the federal Directorate, registrars general of the federal member states, the Banadir registrar, local government (district) registrars with deputy registrars for villages and rural areas, and embassies and consulates

systems.system: diiwaanka qoyska (family register and residence registration)
systems.tiers: each district registers every household and person resident in it and keeps a family book

note: The text is Somali statute and states what the law requires, not what is in operation. No fact is taken on how the record is made, because the law does not say where the digital entry happens: it has the informant's data written on a prescribed form and signed (article 20), the Directorate preparing registers and distributing them to all offices (article 10), the local registrar sending copies of his registers to the Directorate within 30 working days (article 39) and keeping a printed copy of what he sent (article 45). Births are to be registered within a year and other events within 30 working days, free of charge; health facilities, midwives and vaccinators carry a duty to notify births (article 24).
